'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
***A [[United States]] convoy consisting of 40 trucks and armored vehicles enters northeastern [[Syria]] from [[Iraq]] via the [[Al Waleed border crossing|Al Waleed crossing]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/middle-east/1611293792-us-military-convoy-enters-northeast-syria-report (i24 News)]
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**[[2021 Baghdad bombings]]
***A [[suicide bombing|suicide attack]] at an open market in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], kills at least 32 people and injures 110 others. Attacks have been rare in the country since the 2017 military defeat of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]], making this incident one of the deadliest since then. [https://www.reuters.com/article/BigStory12/idUSKBN29Q0W8 (Reuters)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**The [[Central African Republic]] government declares a 15-day [[state of emergency]] after rebels attempt to surround and [[blockade]] the capital [[Bangui]]. Pro-[[François Bozizé]] loyalists and [[anti-balaka]] militias now control around two-thirds of the war torn nation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/21/c-africa-declares-emergency-as-rebels-try-to-oust-president (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
***Organisers announce that the [[Glastonbury Festival]] has been cancelled for the second consecutive year due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/music/2021/jan/21/glastonbury-2021-officially-cancelled-due-to-covid-pandemic (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic#Impact on culture and entertainment|Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on entertainment]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
**[[Dubai]] suspends all entertainment permits issued by the [[Emirates of the United Arab Emirates|emirate]] for establishments due to an increase in violations of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] health protocols. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/covid-19-rules-dubai-suspends-entertainment-activities (''Khaleej Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182]]
**[[Indonesia]]n authorities, led by [[Ministry of Transportation (Indonesia)|Transportation Minister]] [[Budi Karya Sumadi]], officially end the search for remaining victims and debris from [[Sriwijaya Air]] [[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182|Flight 182]], which crashed into the [[Java Sea]] on January 9, killing all 62 people on board. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/indonesia-ends-search-for-crashed-planes-victims-debris/2021/01/21/456a485e-5be8-11eb-a849-6f9423a75ffd_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2021 Kharkiv fire]]
**Fifteen people are killed and eleven others injured in a fire at a [[nursing home]] in [[Kharkiv]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55755600 (BBC News)]
*Five people are killed in a fire at a [[Serum Institute of India]] facility in [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-55753586 (BBC News)]
*A truck carrying sticks of [[Gelignite|gelatin]] explodes at a boulder-crushing facility in [[Abbalagere]] in [[Shimoga district|Shivamogga district]], [[Karnataka]], [[India]], killing eight workers. [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/loud-nise-shimoga-karnataka-supersonic-jet-earthquake-1761516-2021-01-21 (''India Today'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama]]
*****[[Governor of Alabama|Alabama Governor]] [[Kay Ivey]] extends the [[Alabama|statewide]] mask mandate to March 5. [https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Ivey-expected-to-announce-fate-of-Alabama-mask-15887024.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Tennessee]] reports their first two cases of a more contagious variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] that was first identified in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.wsmv.com/news/tennessee/2-cases-of-covid-19-variant-strain-found-in-tennessee/article_de714fc6-5c23-11eb-b765-1f19d5a2b4e4.html (WSMV-TV)]
****[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
*****[[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs an executive order requiring usage of masks in airports and on airplanes, trains and buses. [https://apnews.com/article/biden-sign-measure-mask-use-travel-01676a2c85386aa741d83d977e895353 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] reports a record 22,339 newly confirmed cases and 1,809 deaths in the past 24 hours. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/mexico-posts-daily-highs-pandemic-cases-deaths-75417956 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Trinidad and Tobago]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Trinidad and Tobago]] reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a person returning from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://trinidadexpress.com/newsextra/t-t-records-first-covid-19-variant-case/article_13288238-5c1b-11eb-a79b-0f256c309367.html (''Daily Express'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record of 221 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,686. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/325_DGS_boletim_20210121.pdf (DGS)]
****The [[Government of Portugal|government]] announces the closure of all schools, kindergartens and universities for two weeks beginning tomorrow due to an increase in [[Coronavirus disease|COVID-19]] cases, as well as the emergence of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]. [https://www.theportugalnews.com/news/2021-01-21/government-likely-to-close-all-schools-tomorrow/57841 (''The Portugal News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Hungary]] approves the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine]] and [[Russia]]'s [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V]] vaccine, becoming the first [[European Union]] member state to approve the Russian vaccine. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55747623 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|Dutch House of Representatives]] votes to impose a curfew from 9.00 p.m. to 4.30 a.m. beginning January 23. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/01/21/dutch-parliament-backs-plans-for-a-9pm-4-30am-covid-curfew?utm_source=news.google.com&utm_campaign=feeds_news&utm_medium=referral (Euronews)] [https://www.rtlnieuws.nl/nieuws/politiek/artikel/5210005/tweede-kamer-akkoord-over-avondklok-van-21-uur-tot (RTL Nieuws)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Mayor of Moscow|Moscow Mayor]] [[Sergei Sobyanin]] announces that as part of an easing of COVID-19 restrictions, museums and libraries will reopen beginning tomorrow, while theatres and cinemas will be allowed to accommodate more patrons. In addition, colleges, sports schools and children's clubs will resume in-person attendance, but university students will continue studying remotely. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/01/21/moscow-announces-significant-easing-of-virus-restrictions-a72682 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] reports a record 44,357 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,456,675. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/vida/20210121/6189163/sanidad-record-contagios-coronavirus-muertes-espana-covid.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 346 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 27,203. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5343086/rekor-346-kematian-kasus-corona-di-indonesia-21-januari-tambah-11703 (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reopens to foreign tourists after a nearly 10-month pandemic closure, however tourists are required to receive multiple [[COVID-19 testing|testings]] and follow [[quarantine]] measures that have been put in place. [https://apnews.com/article/travel-sri-lanka-accommodations-asia-coronavirus-pandemic-856c0285aeac28d7645b3e85ac71c84a (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]]'s Food and Drug Administration approves the emergency use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]]. 50,000 doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] are expected to arrive in February. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2054799/astrazeneca-vaccine-approved-50-000-doses-due-in-february (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
****[[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] receives a dose of the [[Russia]]n-made [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine, a day after the usage of vaccines for people over the age of 60 was approved by the [[Argentina|country]]'s health regulator. [https://www.lanacion.com.ar/politica/coronavirus-argentina-alberto-fernandez-recibio-primera-dosis-nid2578083 (''La Nacion'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]]n [[Minister in the Presidency]] [[Jackson Mthembu]] dies due to [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/21/africa/south-africa-minister-covid-death-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[European Union–Russia relations]]
** The [[European Court of Human Rights]] rules that [[Russia]] was responsible for a series of human rights violations during its [[Russo-Georgian War|2008 war with Georgia]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/21/russia-human-rights-violation-georgia-war-echr-ruling?fbclid=IwAR0E_DbjhPJaixgOGvkmh-ZA5tY9XveD-bnhUw0oEy29ZlghmpctVMdMXEo (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Syria–United States relations]]
** [[Bashar al-Jaafari]], [[Permanent Representative of Syria to the United Nations]], called on [[Biden]] to change US foreign policy in [[Syria]], which is nearing 10 years of [[Syrian civil war|civil war]]. During a session of the UN Security Council, Jaafari accused the United States of using the multi-sided war to steal the country's oil reserves and other natural resources.  [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/syria-ambassador-un-calls-us-withdraw-troops-stop-acts-aggression (''Middle East Eye'')]
'''Law and crime'''
*[[Japanese nationality law]]
**The [[Tokyo District Court]] upholds a ban on [[dual citizenship]] of Japan and another country, rejecting appeals for [[damages]] claiming that the law was unconstitutional. [https://japantoday.com/category/national/japan-court-upholds-ban-on-dual-citizenship (AFP via ''Japan Today'')]
*A [[Vatican City|Vatican]] tribunal convicts two former executives of the [[Institute for the Works of Religion|Institute for Religious Works]] (the IOR, commonly known as the Vatican bank) on embezzlement and money-laundering charges. [[Angelo Caloia]], who was president of the IOR from 1999 to 2009; and two lawyers who had acted as IOR consultants, were found guilty of arranging to profit from the sale of Vatican properties. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/vatican-convicts-ex-bank-chief-in-property-embezzlement-scam/2021/01/21/f7e442a0-5c0b-11eb-a849-6f9423a75ffd_story.html (AP)]
'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidency of Joe Biden]], [[Efforts to impeach Joe Biden]]
**[[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] [[United States House of Representatives|Representative]] [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] introduces six articles of [[impeachment]] against newly-inaugurated [[President of the United States]] [[Joe Biden]], alleging an [[Biden–Ukraine conspiracy theory|"abuse of power"]] when Biden served as [[Barack Obama]]'s [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/biden-impeachment-taylor-greene-qanon-b1790965.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
**[[Prime Minister of Mongolia|Mongolian Prime Minister]] [[Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh]] resigns a day after thousands in [[Ulaanbaatar]] protested against the way authorities behaved with a [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]-infected mother and her newborn baby. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/mongolians-protest-covid-19-curbs-ulaanbaatar-14011868 (CNA)]
*[[2020–21 Rideau Hall workplace review]]
**[[Julie Payette]] resigns as [[Governor General of Canada]] following a review that cites allegations of a toxic work environment at [[Rideau Hall]]. [[Chief Justice of Canada]] [[Richard Wagner (judge)|Richard Wagner]] will carry out the duties of that office as [[Administrator of the government#Canada|Administrator of Canada]] until [[Monarchy of Canada|the Crown]] appoints a new Governor General. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/governor-general-payette-step-down-1.5882675 (CBC)]
*[[Politics of Palau]]
**[[Surangel Whipps Jr.]] assumes the office of [[President of Palau]] succeeding [[Thomas Remengesau Jr.]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/18/palaus-new-president-vows-to-stand-up-to-bully-china (''The Guardian'')]
'''Science and technology'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[United States federal judge|United States district judge]] for the [[United States District Court for the Western District of Washington|Western District of Washington]] [[Barbara Jacobs Rothstein]] rejects a lawsuit filed by [[Parler]] requesting reinstatement on [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-amazon-com-parler-idUSKBN29Q2T3 (Reuters)]
**[[United States House Committee on Oversight and Reform|House Oversight Committee]] chairwoman [[Carolyn Maloney]] calls for the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] to investigate [[Parler]] for their role in the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/parler-online-fbi-investigation-trump-b1790955.html (''The Independent'')]

***[[International Olympic Committee]] [[President of the International Olympic Committee|President]] [[Thomas Bach]] says that the [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympics]] will be held in July, despite a state of emergency currently being declared in [[Tokyo]].
